class.name: WeatherMap3D
class.brief_description: One weather state for a region of the world: wind, cloud, rain and the water rain leaves on surfaces.
class.description: A square map of weather cells, [member extent] metres wide, that follows the camera (or [member follow_target]), after the weather map of Guerrilla's Nubis clouds. Each cell holds the mean wind at 10 m, cloud cover and type, the rain rate, and the water that rain has left on surfaces: a film up to [member surface_storage], then puddles. The film dries by evaporation (Penman's wind function, from [member temperature] and [member humidity]) and puddles also drain. The weather comes from the base settings, which the map eases toward over [member transition_time]; cloud cover broken up by noise that drifts with the wind aloft; an optional [member painted_map]; and storms ([method add_storm]) that drift with the wind and bring a rain core and a downburst outflow. Wind follows the log law with height over [member roughness_length], plus gusts from the Kaimal spectrum (IEC 61400-1) carried by the mean wind (Taylor's frozen turbulence), so every reader sees the same gust at the same place and time. Near the ground it is sheltered by plant canopies and obstacles (see [member shelter_enabled]) and carried in gust patches of a few metres ([member gust_patch_size]). Readers: [method get_wind_at] and the other [code]get_*_at[/code] methods; [PhysXWaterSurface3D] with [member PhysXWaterSurface3D.follow_weather]; [PhysXCloth3D] and [PhysXHair3D] (their [code]weather_wind[/code]); and any shader, raster or path traced, through these global uniforms (added at run time when the project does not declare them): - [code]weather_wind_map[/code] ([code]sampler2D[/code]): mean wind at 10 m in m/s (RG, x and z), cloud cover (B), cloud type (A). - [code]weather_state_map[/code] ([code]sampler2D[/code]): rain in mm/h (R), wetness 0 to 1 (G), puddle depth in mm (B), film in mm (A). - [code]weather_map_rect[/code] ([code]vec4[/code]): the map's world rect, x and z of its corner, then its size. A world point's map UV is [code](world.xz - rect.xy) / rect.zw[/code]. - [code]weather_gusts[/code] ([code]sampler2D[/code], [constant GUST_COUNT] by 1): per gust wave, its wavenumber along and across the base wind (rad/m), amplitude per unit sigma and phase. The first [constant GUSTS_PER_AXIS] are along the local wind, the next across it, the last vertical. - [code]weather_wind_info[/code] ([code]vec4[/code]): base wind direction (x, z), sigma_u over the 10 m wind, and [member roughness_length]. - [code]weather_ground_height[/code] ([code]float[/code]): [member ground_height]. - [code]weather_shelter_map[/code] ([code]sampler2D[/code]) and [code]weather_shelter_rect[/code] ([code]vec4[/code]): per cell of the shelter square, canopy height (R), Cionco's coefficient (G), the lee factor (B) and the height of the obstacle setting it (A); the rect has zero size while [member shelter_enabled] is off. - [code]weather_patch_info[/code] ([code]vec4[/code]): how far the gust patches have travelled (x, z), one over [member gust_patch_size], and their strength over the noise's spread. [method get_wind_shader_code] returns shader code that reads all of these and gives the same wind as [method get_wind_at]. Readers on worker threads must not call the getters while the map updates. From C++, take [code]get_snapshot()[/code] on the main thread instead: a read-only copy of the rain, cloud cover and cloud shadow with the parameters to sample them, whose [code]rain_at()[/code], [code]cloud_cover_at()[/code] and [code]sun_visibility_at()[/code] answer as [method get_rain_at], [method get_cloud_cover_at] and [method get_sun_visibility_at] did when it was taken. Its arrays share the map's buffers, so while a snapshot is held each weather update copies them once. Clouds: a layer from [member cloud_base_height], shaped from the same cover and type by 3D noise (Nubis), drawn by [WeatherSkyMaterial] when the environment's sky uses it, and shadowing [member sun_light] through a baked cloud shadow. Under path tracing, enable [member Environment.pathtracing_sky_shader_enabled] so camera rays see the clouds at full detail. The last [WeatherMap3D] to enter the tree is the one the other nodes read.

method.name: add_canopy
method.description: Adds a round stand of plants (world x, z centre, radius and canopy height in metres) and returns its id. [param density] is Cionco's attenuation coefficient: about 1 for open orchards, 2 to 3 for crops and most forests, 4 for dense stands (Cionco 1978). Under the canopy the wind falls off as [code]u(hc) exp(a (z / hc - 1))[/code]; above it the log law starts from a displaced ground at 0.7 hc with roughness 0.1 hc (Raupach 1994). Takes effect at the next shelter bake (see [method rebake_shelter]).

method.name: add_shelter_box
method.description: Adds a solid obstacle (a building, a wall) as a world box and returns its id. Downwind of it the wind near the ground drops to 0.15 of the open wind in a cavity about 2 heights long (Hosker 1984), then recovers over about 6 heights: 0.8 at 10 heights, nearly all at 20 (Heisler and DeWalle 1988). The lee fades out above the obstacle's height. Visible [VisualInstance3D] nodes in the [code]weather_shelter[/code] group are added the same way, from their bounding boxes, at each bake.

method.name: add_storm
method.description: Adds a storm centred on [param position] (world x, z) and returns its id. Its rain core has [param radius] metres and peaks at [param rain_rate] mm/h; its downburst outflow (Oseguera and Bowles 1988) blows outward, strongest at about 1.12 times [param radius] with [param outflow] m/s. It drifts with the wind aloft, grows in and fades out over [param lifetime] seconds of weather time ([code]0[/code] or less: until removed).

method.name: advance
method.description: Runs the weather forward by [param seconds] of weather time at once (in steps of a minute): storms drift, the base state eases, surfaces wet and dry.

method.name: clear_precipitation_extinction
method.description: Removes [param source]'s haze. When the last source clears, the environment's fog is put back as it was.

method.name: clear_shelter
method.description: Removes every canopy and shelter box added from code.

method.name: clear_storms
method.description: Removes every storm.

method.name: clear_surface_water_source
method.description: Stops the water delivered by [param owner] (see [method set_surface_water_source]); the precipitation reaches the ground there again. Sources whose owner is freed are dropped on their own.

method.name: get_air_humidity
method.description: The relative humidity the cells use now (0..1): [member humidity] eased over [member transition_time].

method.name: get_air_temperature
method.description: The air temperature the cells use now (C): [member temperature] eased over [member transition_time].

method.name: get_canopy_closure_at
method.description: The share of the sky the canopy closes over [param position] (0..1), from the shelter canopy there (see [method add_canopy] and [member canopy_map]): its attenuation coefficient taken as a leaf area index through Beer's law with an extinction of 0.5 (Monsi and Saeki 1953), about 0.4 for an open orchard and 0.7 for a forest. [code]0[/code] where there is no canopy. Snow interception and the light under the trees can follow it.

method.name: get_canopy_height_at
method.description: The height (m) of the shelter canopy over [param position], [code]0[/code] where there is none.

method.name: get_cloud_cover_at
method.description: Cloud cover at [param position], 0 (clear) to 1 (overcast).

method.name: get_cloud_density_at
method.description: Extinction of the cloud layer at [param position], per metre (0 in clear air). The base shape only: the sky erodes edges a little further with detail noise.

method.name: get_cloud_shadow_texture
method.description: The last cloud shadow bake: the sun's transmittance over [member cloud_shadow_extent], in the plane of [member sun_light], sRGB encoded. The map gives it to that light as its projector.

method.name: get_cloud_top_at
method.description: The top of the cloud the sky draws over [param position]'s x and z (world y, metres). It is the base plus the column's height for its cloud type: a quarter of [member cloud_thickness] for stratus, all of it for cumulus, and up to three times it in a storm's core, where the type reaches 0.9. [WeatherLightning3D] takes its flash rate from this height.

method.name: get_cloud_type_at
method.description: Cloud type at [param position], 0 (stratus) to 1 (cumulonimbus), as in the Nubis weather map.

method.name: get_day_of_year
method.description: Day of the year (1 to 365) of the [member sky_clock]'s date, or [member season_day] without one.

method.name: get_gust_texture
method.description: The texture published as [code]weather_gusts[/code].

method.name: get_map_rect
method.description: The world rect the map covers now (x and z of its corner, and its size).

method.name: get_mean_wind_at
method.description: The mean wind at 10 m at [param position] (x, z, m/s), without gusts.

method.name: get_precipitation_extinction_at
method.description: The sum of every source's extinction at [param position] (1/m), with each layer's fall-off with height and each local source's edge.

method.name: get_puddle_at
method.description: Puddle depth at [param position], in millimetres.

method.name: get_rain_at
method.description: Rain rate at [param position], in mm/h.

method.name: get_season
method.description: The season at [member ground_height] on [method get_day_of_year]: one state for every system that follows the year (trees, ground plants, snow, water). Keys: [code]day_of_year[/code]; [code]latitude_deg[/code]; [code]photoperiod_h[/code], day length (Forsythe et al. 1995); [code]temperature[/code], the day's mean, C; [code]forcing[/code], growing degree days above 5 C since 1 January; [code]chilling[/code], days with a mean of 0 to 5 C since 1 November (Cannell and Smith 1983); [code]senescence[/code], from the first day after midsummer the day is under 13.2 h, the sum of max(0, 20 - T) (photoperiod / 13.2)² (Delpierre et al. 2009); [code]snow_depth[/code] (m), [code]snow_cover[/code] (0 to 1) and [code]snow_line_m[/code] (m), from a degree-day snowpack built since 1 August; [code]soil_frost[/code], freezing degree days since 1 August under no snow, thawed back by warm days (K days); [code]soil_moisture[/code], 0 to 1 of the soil's water capacity (a Thornthwaite and Mather bucket). The sums run over a climatological year from [member climate] (a harmonic of its January and July means, as TerrainGenerator3D's water balance), shifted by [member season_anomaly], so any date is right at once. Cached until the day changes or the anomaly moves 0.25 K. Ground snow at a place is [code]SnowCover3D[/code]'s; this is the site's.

method.name: get_season_at_height
method.description: [method get_season] at another height (m), with the climate's lapse rate. Not cached.

method.name: get_shelter_at
method.description: The mean wind at [param position] and that height (below 0: from [member ground_height]) over the wind on open ground at the same height: canopies and the lee of obstacles, 0 to 1.

method.name: get_shelter_bake_time
method.description: How long the last shelter bake took, in milliseconds.

method.name: get_shelter_rect
method.description: The shelter square's world rect (x and z of its corner, then its size), as published in [code]weather_shelter_rect[/code].

method.name: get_shelter_texture
method.description: The texture published as [code]weather_shelter_map[/code].

method.name: get_state_texture
method.description: The texture published as [code]weather_state_map[/code].

method.name: get_storm_count
method.description: The number of storms.

method.name: get_sun_visibility_at
method.description: How much of the sun reaches [param position] through the clouds, 0 to 1, from the last cloud shadow bake. 1 outside the baked square or without [member sun_light].

method.name: get_weather_time
method.description: Seconds of weather time since the map started ([member time_scale] times the clock).

method.name: get_wetness_at
method.description: How wet surfaces are at [param position]: the water film over [member surface_storage], 1 where water stands.

method.name: get_wind_at
method.description: Air velocity at [param position] in m/s: the mean wind on the log law at [param height_above_ground] metres (when negative, the height above [member ground_height]), plus gusts.

method.name: get_wind_shader_code
method.description: Shader code that computes the same wind as [method get_wind_at]: the global uniform declarations, then [code]vec3 weather_wind(vec3 world_position, float height_above_ground)[/code]. Paste it into a spatial or canvas shader (or build it in) and leave out any global uniforms the shader already declares.

method.name: get_wind_texture
method.description: The texture published as [code]weather_wind_map[/code].

method.name: rain_fraction
method.description: The share of precipitation that falls as rain at [param celsius] and relative [param humidity] (0..1): the complement of the snowfall fraction of Jennings et al. (2018). Only this share wets surfaces as it falls; the rest is snow.

method.name: rebake_shelter
method.description: Bakes the shelter square now. It also bakes by itself when canopies or boxes change, when the camera has moved an eighth of [member shelter_extent], and when the wind has turned by about 3 degrees. Call it after moving nodes in the [code]weather_shelter[/code] group.

method.name: remove_canopy
method.description: Removes a canopy added with [method add_canopy].

method.name: remove_shelter_box
method.description: Removes a box added with [method add_shelter_box].

method.name: remove_storm
method.description: Removes the storm with this [param id].

method.name: set_precipitation_extinction
method.description: Haze from falling or blowing precipitation, pushed by [param source] (a snowfall or rain node). Calling it again for the same source replaces that source's haze. [param sigma] is the extinction in 1/m; the visibility is about 3.912 / sigma. With [param height_scale] above 0, it is a layer over the ground whose density falls as exp(-(y - ground) / height_scale), as blowing snow does; otherwise it is the same at every height. [param albedo] is the share of light scattered rather than absorbed. With [param radius] above 0, it covers a circle around [param centre], and a layer's ground is [param centre]'s height (pass the ground under the camera so the layer follows the terrain); otherwise it covers the whole map over [member ground_height]. Layers turn on the environment's volumetric fog with [member Environment.volumetric_fog_ambient_inject] at 1 (sky-lit snow reads white) unless the project set its own. Sources add up. With [member drive_environment_fog], the uniform part goes into the environment's exponential fog, coloured by the sky, and each layer into a lit [FogVolume] that the volumetric fog draws within 300 m of the camera. The path tracer reads both. See [code]docs/ideas/weather.md[/code], "Precipitation haze".

method.name: set_surface_water_source
method.description: Water that [param owner] delivers to the ground over [param rect] (world X, Z), in mm/h on a [param resolution] square of [param rates] (row-major in Z then X), in place of the precipitation the map would put there: a [SnowCover3D] passes its runoff (the rain through the pack and its melt), so snow wets surfaces when it melts, not when it falls. The values are copied; call again with new ones. Several sources add up.

method.name: snap_to_settings
method.description: Jumps the eased weather to the settings at once, without a transition (for example when a scene loads).

method.name: update_cloud_shadow
method.description: Bakes the cloud shadow now and waits for it. The map otherwise bakes it on the worker threads every [member cloud_shadow_interval] seconds.

members.member: A map of plant canopies over [member canopy_map_rect]: canopy height in red (metres in a float texture, else times [member canopy_map_max_height]) and Cionco's attenuation coefficient over 4 in green. For vegetation systems that place whole forests.
The canopy height that red 1 stands for in an 8-bit [member canopy_map].
The world rect [member canopy_map] covers (x and z of its corner, then its size).

The climate of the place for [method get_season]: a [code]ClimateRecipe[/code], or any resource with its property names (temperature_january, temperature_july, lapse_rate_january, lapse_rate_july, reference_height, precipitation, precipitation_seasonality, precipitation_peak_month, rain_snow_threshold, daily_temperature_spread, melt_factor, soil_capacity, latitude). Without one, a temperate default (3 C in January, 22 C in July, 900 mm).
Height of the cloud base, in metres above y = 0.
Cloud cover, 0 (clear) to 1 (overcast). With [member cloud_variation], it is how much of the sky is cloud, in patches.
Scale on the clouds' extinction. At [code]1[/code], the measured values: about 0.04 per metre in stratus, up to 0.1 in cumulus (Frostbite, 2016).
Size of the cloud cover patches, in metres.
Width of the square of ground the cloud shadow covers around the camera (or [member follow_target]), in metres. Beyond it, the sun is not shadowed by clouds.
Real seconds between cloud shadow bakes. Between bakes, the shadow slides with the clouds.
Texels along each side of the cloud shadow. Each bake marches 12 steps through the layer per texel, on the worker threads (about 26 ms of CPU at 256 on four cores).
Size of one tile of the 3D shape noise, in metres. Single clouds are about a quarter of it across.
Depth of the cloud layer for cumulus ([member cloud_type] 0.7), in metres. Stratus is a quarter of it; cumulonimbus (type above 0.8, as storms make) towers up to five times it.
Cloud type, 0 (stratus) to 1 (cumulonimbus).
How far the drifting noise moves the cloud cover up or down from [member cloud_cover]. [code]0[/code] gives an even sky.
The haze from [method set_precipitation_extinction] drives the environment's fog and volumetric fog, while the game runs. Off, the sources only answer [method get_precipitation_extinction_at].
Width of the map, in metres.
The node the map stays centred on. Empty: the viewport's camera.
Height of the ground, for [method get_wind_at] when no height above ground is given.
Scale on the turbulence. [code]1[/code] gives the measured turbulence intensity for [member roughness_length], 1 / ln(10 / z0) at 10 m.

The size of the gust patches that sweep across fields and water (honami over crops, cat's paws on water), in metres. They travel at about 1.8 times the wind at the top of a crop (Raupach, Finnigan and Brunet 1996) and fade out above twice their size.
How much the gust patches vary the wind near the ground: the standard deviation of the speed over its mean (0.3 to 0.5 at the top of crops and forests, Finnigan 2000). [code]0[/code] turns them off.
Relative humidity of the air, 0 to 1. Drier air dries surfaces faster. While it rains, the air is taken as at least 97%.
An authored weather map over [member painted_map_rect], in the Nubis channels: R cloud cover (replaces [member cloud_cover]), G a scale on [member rain_rate], B cloud type.
The world rect [member painted_map] covers (x and z of its corner, and its size, in metres).
If [code]true[/code], the map publishes the global shader uniforms listed in the description.
How fast puddles drain into the ground and gutters, in mm/h, on top of evaporation.
The deepest puddles get, in millimetres.
Rain rate where the cloud is thick, in mm/h (2.5 is light rain, 10 heavy, 50 a downpour).
Cells along each side of the map.
Aerodynamic roughness length z0 of the ground, in metres: about 0.0002 over the sea, 0.03 over open land, 0.5 to 1 over a town. It sets how the wind slows near the ground and how gusty it is.

How much warmer (K) this year runs than the [member climate]: the live air temperature's departure from the climate's mean for the day, averaged over about a month of weather time while the map runs. Set it for a warm or cold year.
Day of the year for [method get_season] when there is no [member sky_clock] (135 is 15 May).

Wind near the ground drops inside plant canopies ([method add_canopy], [member canopy_map]) and in the lee of obstacles ([method add_shelter_box], the [code]weather_shelter[/code] group), on a square of [member shelter_extent] around the camera. Applies to [method get_wind_at] and, through [code]weather_shelter_map[/code], to shaders.
The width of the shelter square around the camera, in metres. Past it there is no shelter.
Cells across the shelter square (2 m cells by default).
The [SkyClock] whose date and latitude [method get_season] uses.

The [DirectionalLight3D] the clouds shadow. The map sets that light's [member Light3D.light_projector], [member DirectionalLight3D.projector_size] and [member DirectionalLight3D.projector_offset] to its cloud shadow, which darkens the ground in raster and path traced rendering alike, and clears the projector again when the map leaves the tree. Empty: no cloud shadows.
Water a surface holds as a film before it collects in puddles, in millimetres.
Air temperature, in degrees Celsius, for evaporation.
Weather seconds per real second: storms, transitions, wetting and drying run this much faster than the clock (60 makes a game hour a real minute). Gusts always run in real time.
Time constant over which the weather eases toward changed settings, in weather seconds. [code]0[/code] changes at once.
How often the cells are refreshed, per second. Gusts are evaluated every frame regardless.
The way the wind blows toward, as x and z.
Mean wind speed at 10 m above the ground, in m/s.

constants.constant: Gust waves for each of the three wind axes.
Gust waves in all: the width of the [code]weather_gusts[/code] texture.
